bullets.title: META: Citi upgrades to Buy $800 PT; Muse Wonder launch drives +3-4% rally, multiple analysts raise targets
bullets.body: Citi's Ron Josey upgraded META to Buy with $800 PT (22x 2027E GAAP EPS of $36.92); Pivotal lifted to $930 from $790; KeyBanc and Yorkville maintain $900. Muse Wonder and Wonder Full outperform Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI GPT-6 on select coding/agentic benchmarks. Monetization paths include Muse Code ($50-$200/month) and consumer subscriptions ($20-$100/month); infrastructure includes 5GW+ superclusters at $50-60B upfront CapEx.

bullets.title: Semis under broad pressure: SOX -8% on CXMT DRAM claims, NVDA China share loss, AI financing fears
bullets.body: The SOX fell ~8% on the week and SOXX dropped 2.3% pre-market: STX -7.9%, WDC -7.6%, MU -5.1%, ARM -3.2%, MRVL -3.4%, SMCI -3.0%. CXMT's claimed 4F² DRAM breakthrough pressured memory (SK Hynix -10%, Samsung -7% on KOSPI); analysts view the claims as overstated with unproven yields vs. Samsung's 2028 target. NVDA China market share declining amid export controls and Huawei competition; Rubin shipment expectations reportedly cut from ~10K to ~5K units.

bullets.title: JPM raises cloud DC capex to +85% in 2026 / +70% in 2027; ANET/CLS/CRDO key networking beneficiaries
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised CSP cloud DC capex estimates to +85% for 2026 (from +80%) and +70% for 2027 (from +50%), implying $270B+ and $400B+ dollar increases. GOOGL and META lead at 120%+ and ~100% YoY growth respectively. The shift from accelerator capacity toward networking is structurally bullish for ANET, CLS, and CRDO; NVDA confirmed Rubin in full production with cable-free tray and Spectrum-X CPO shipping this year.

bullets.title: MSFT: CIO survey shows 30% preference for GenAI spend; Azure leads at 79% usage vs AWS 66%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's 3Q26 CIO survey shows MSFT cited by 30% of CIOs as the vendor most likely to gain incremental GenAI spend (up from 27% in Q2). Azure usage leads at 79% vs AWS 66% and GCP 43%; Azure and AWS both expecting +15% spending in 2026. 64% of CIOs prefer buying AI capabilities vs. building, favoring MSFT, CRM, NOW, ORCL, and SNOW; Hedgeye maintains MSFT as an explicit long.

bullets.title: AAPL at 52-week high (+40.5% YTD); launches HomeView smart home hub at $299
bullets.body: Apple launched HomeView, a smart home display priced at $299 featuring facial recognition and an enhanced AI Siri; pre-orders begin Oct 13 with general availability Nov 13. The device is unavailable in the EU due to Siri AI regulatory restrictions. AAPL hit a 52-week high at $344.50, up 40.5% YTD; Hedgeye maintains explicit bullish stance.

bullets.title: NOW: Oppenheimer raises PT to $165 from $140; 3Q whisper strong but 4Q guide is the real test
bullets.body: Field checks show healthy demand and strong AI pricing uplift; 3Q CRPO whisper is $13.8B+ (~22% y/y, ~250bps upside). However, customers are requiring clearer AI ROI before expanding deployments, sales cycles are elongating, and federal demand remains weak. The consensus has shifted from fundamentals to valuation — a strong 3Q print alone may not move the stock; 4Q guidance and AI revenue evidence are the key catalysts.

bullets.title: SHOP hits 52-week high (C$254, +20.2% YTD, +13% w/w) on AI-commerce momentum
bullets.body: Shopify reached a new 52-week high at C$253.99, up 4.2% intraday and 13% on the week. Cantor Fitzgerald raised its SHOP target to $158 from $145 (Neutral). JPMorgan is hosting an expert call with Shopify Platinum Partner Zettler Digital on Oct 19 covering AI-commerce strategy (Sidekick & Muse), merchant adoption, and Shopify Payments trends.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI PC launch targeted Q1 2027; FY27 record bookings expected
bullets.body: Take-Two plans a GTA VI PC launch in Q1 2027 per GamesBeat citing four industry sources, following the console launch on November 19, 2026. Management raised FY26 net bookings guidance to $6.4-6.5B (from $6.05-6.15B) and expects record FY27 net bookings. Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.46 beat consensus of $0.94; Q2 net bookings of $1.96B beat consensus of $1.73B.

bullets.title: AMZN/GOOGL outperform internet cohort; Cantor raises AMZN PT to $320
bullets.body: Internet names +2% overall with AMZN +4% and GOOGL +2% leading; CART and RDDT each +8%, U +7%. Cantor Fitzgerald raised AMZN target to $320 from $310 (Overweight) and maintains GOOGL at $420 (Overweight), expecting cloud acceleration and healthy margin expansion in C3Q26. AMZN/GOOGL/META trade at 20x/17x/23x 2026E EPS respectively.

bullets.title: T and VZ: Bernstein downgrades T to Market Perform, cuts PT to $24 on Starlink competitive threat
bullets.body: Bernstein downgraded AT&T to Market Perform from Outperform and cut the PT to $24 from $25, citing ongoing Starlink competitive pressure in broadband/wireless and expected Q4 seasonality headwinds. T and VZ each fell ~10-11% on Oct 9 following SpaceX wireless spectrum announcement; Citi sees 12-month recovery opportunity but acknowledges near-term downside.

bullets.title: NFLX: Citi bullish ($800 PT context); Huber downgrades to Underweight, cuts PT to $70; secures 2030 World Cup Spain rights
bullets.body: Huber Research downgraded NFLX to Underweight from Overweight and slashed its PT to $70 from $85, implying ~1% downside from the $70.61 price (vs. consensus $91.98). Separately, NFLX secured rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup in Spain and Andorra covering all 104 matches with one free match per day. Hedgeye's risk range flags NFLX as bearish with a $65-$71 buy/sell range.

bullets.title: AMD: Fermi signs credit support agreement covering 222MW for TensorWave lease; project financing expected 4Q26-1Q27
bullets.body: Fermi Inc. signed a credit support agreement with AMD to backstop TensorWave's first data center lease (222 MW utility power), with a framework supporting up to 650 MW for full expansion. UBS maintains Neutral on Fermi (FRMI) with a $6 PT (16x 2029 EBITDA); project financing expected in 4Q26 or early 1Q27. Rising interest rates have complicated data center financing, and clarity on total build cost and NOI is still needed.

bullets.title: TSEM & SMTC partnership expanding; TER acquires $300M FORM equity stake for next-gen testing
bullets.body: TSEM and SMTC expanded their SiGe foundry capacity partnership amid explosive growth in optical interconnect demand. Separately, Teradyne (TER) is purchasing $300M in FormFactor (FORM) equity to accelerate next-gen semiconductor testing collaboration. Analyst Klein views these as positive fundamental signals amid the broader sector selloff.

bullets.title: CVNA: 22V technical analyst sees major top forming; technical score falls to 0
bullets.body: 22V Research's chart technician downgraded CVNA's technical score to 0 from 1, noting feeble momentum indicators and characterizing the stock as forming a 'big top.' The analyst expects the stock to move importantly lower from current levels.

bullets.title: ADBE downgraded to Hold at HSBC, PT cut to $267 from $310
bullets.body: HSBC downgraded Adobe to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $267 from $310, citing narrowing performance gaps between frontier AI models and growing developer enthusiasm for cheaper alternatives as headwinds to Adobe's AI product positioning.

bullets.title: DKNG: Indiana sports betting GGR +68% y/y in September but handle -1%; hold rate elevated at 8.6%
bullets.body: DraftKings posted Indiana September sports betting GGR of +68% y/y but handle fell -1% y/y; hold rate of 8.6% was up 360bps y/y. DKNG's market share held at 36% vs. 37% the prior year. Fanatics was the standout, with GGR +51% and handle +17% y/y, gaining market share to 7% from 6%.

bullets.title: Hedgeye: Bullish MSFT/AAPL/META/SNOW; bearish ORCL; trimmed META ahead of CPI
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Keith McCullough reduced Real-Time Alerts to one long on Monday, trimming META after a rebound ahead of Wednesday's CPI release (expecting 3.6%, up from 3.4%). Snowflake is identified as a Signal Strength long; Oracle flagged as a potential short with trend breakdown and bearish analyst coverage. Signal Strength longs have declined from 79 to 45 since August 31; shorts increased from 56 to 80.

bullets.title: WDAY acquires C1.ai agentic identity platform; deal expected to close Jan 2027
bullets.body: Workday signed a definitive agreement to acquire C1.ai, an agentic identity platform providing access management across email, CRM, code repositories, finance systems, and cloud infrastructure. Transaction terms were not disclosed; closing expected in Q4 of Workday's FY27 (ending January 31, 2027).

bullets.title: ORCL: Signs $10M/year power deal with El Paso Electric for Project Jupiter data center
bullets.body: Oracle signed an Energy Service agreement with El Paso Electric for Project Jupiter, committing to $10M annually for 10 years regardless of usage, while proposing $55M in direct credits to EPE customers from 2027. Bloom Energy fuel cell microgrids remain the primary power source with no change to plan. Hedgeye separately flags ORCL as a potential short with a trend breakdown.

bullets.title: HUT/powered shell stocks down 27% in 3 months; 22V sees value with HUT best positioned
bullets.body: Powered shell stocks are pricing near-zero pipeline conversion despite a 30GW+ unsited AI capacity gap through 2030. HUT 8 is highlighted as best positioned due to its investment-grade rating, lowest funding costs, and strong TX/LA positioning for Anthropic expansion. Applied Digital has the most significant contracted HPC with 15%+ lease renewal increases; BTDR is flagged as exposed to Ohio moratoriums and litigation.
